diagnoses.rule_anchor: Apply Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(g) as a separate motor-vehicle alternative. Start with its $4,000 ceiling and add the unused amount of the $12,000 § 815.18(3)(d) allowance; under independent asset-exemption evaluation, no other listed asset consumes that allowance. For one debtor, report the lesser of the whole vehicle's value and $16,000.

Apply Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(d) to household goods, furnishings, apparel, jewelry, adornment, appliances, books, musical instruments, firearms, sporting goods, animals, and other qualifying tangible personal property. Report the lesser of the whole asset's value and the applicable $12,000 debtor ceiling; if joint ownership makes the ceiling bind, apply § 815.18(8) to each equal interest and sum the protected interests.
Execution example: When federal exemptions are also allowable, a professionally prescribed personal mobility aid can require separate entries for federal § 522(d)(9), federal § 522(d)(5), and Wisconsin § 815.18(3)(d), each valued independently.
